newsitem.title: USA: Most US spot resids steady to up, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: Most US spot resids steady to up, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly were steady to firmer Friday in sluggish trade, still underpinned by a firm crude market and relatively tight prompt avails, particularly of high sulphur material, sources said.

"The numbers are high, but the market is still fairly tight, particularly for high sulphur, and everyone is looking at crude," said one cash trader, adding as long as crude held, resids were not likely to back off much.
In New York Harbor, one percent was unchanged at about $21.25 a barrel, with early November paper quotes at about $20.50 but higher later after the crude rebound, traders said.
NYH high sulphurs notionally edged higher with still-firm bunkers. NYH three percent gained 50 cents to $19.25-50, with some pegging the level closer to $20.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent held steady in the mid-$20 area, with 50,000 barrels for prompt delivery sold at $20.50 (FOB Houston).
USG one percent notionally slipped 25-50 cents on unconfirmed reports of a 50,000-barrel deal at $19.50 (FOB Miss. River) which some said was below-market.
Gas at the New York City gate firmed another five cents Friday to near the $2.70/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
